title: UK keeps AI safeguards in the maybe pile for Cyber Security BIll
key_facts: UK officials have stopped short of committing to AI-specific measures in the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, despite ministers promising to legislate where necessary.
Senior civil servants told MPs this week the government is still considering amendments to address AI risks, including how serious incidents and near misses are reported.
At Tuesday's committee hearing (13 Oct 2026), chair Liam Byrne said "You can't consider something in a bill. You have to legislate for something in a bill."
AI minister Kanishka Narayan said "We will legislate wherever necessary."
Anthropic research published Monday explored whether AI models could copy themselves between devices; its forecast extrapolates from improving capabilities, not a demonstrated worm.
Consultancy Booz Allen Hamilton warned autonomous AI systems could attack critical operational technology such as water and power.
The UK has a decentralised, sector-specific approach to AI regulation; the EU AI Act took effect in August 2024 in stages; the US has no federal AI-specific law.
quote_evidence: "You can't consider something in a bill. You have to legislate for something in a bill."
Its forecast extrapolates from improving model capabilities, rather than demonstrating a fully autonomous worm spreading across real IoT devices.
why_it_matters_hint: UK binding rules for AI-driven cyber threats remain undecided.
